title: EGA VI. Plans, notations, problèmes ouverts : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a typed page, numbered 31, of a draft on fibre functors (points) of topoi, ending with the étale topos. The numbering 7.9.x and the content match SGA 4 Exposé VIII §7, 'Points du topos étale'. The page seems unrelated to the handwritten EGA VI plans on the neighbouring pages, so it is probably interleaved or misfiled material.

(7.9.1, end) Setting: C is a site with finite projective limits, E = C~ its topos of sheaves, and φ: E → (Ens) a fibre functor, i.e. a functor commuting with colimits and finite limits. C_φ is the category of pairs (Y, ξ) with Y ∈ C and ξ ∈ φ(Ỹ). Y̌ denotes the covariant functor Hom(Ỹ, −) on E.

There is an evident map (*): colim over C_φ^op of Y̌ → φ. By Yoneda, Hom(colim Y̌, φ) = lim Hom(Y̌, φ) = lim φ(Ỹ). The canonical element of this limit is the family (ξ), indexed by the pairs (Y, ξ).

Why the colimit is filtered: C has finite limits, and Y ↦ φ(Ỹ) preserves them. Hence C_φ has finite limits, so C_φ^op has finite colimits and is (pseudo-)filtrant.

Why (*) is bijective: every sheaf F is a colimit of sheaves Ỹ, and φ commutes with colimits. So φ is pro-represented by the pro-object (Ỹ) indexed by (Y, ξ) ∈ C_φ. In modern terms, a point of a topos is the same as a flat (filtering) functor on the site, and the fibre functor is a filtered colimit of corepresentables over the category of elements.

7.9.2: Let Y be an object of E. Points of the slice topos E/Y are the same as pairs (φ, ξ), with φ a point of E and ξ ∈ φ(Y). Given ψ on E/Y, set φ(Z) = ψ(Z × Y → Y). Then ξ is the image of the unique element of ψ(Y), Y being terminal in E/Y, under the diagonal Y → Y × Y. The converse, implicit here, sends (φ, ξ) to ψ(Z → Y) = fibre of φ(Z) → φ(Y) over ξ.

7.9.3: The text starts to apply this to the étale topos of X. This leads to the theorem that every point of X_ét comes from a geometric point (SGA 4 VIII 7.9).
errors: Bijectivity of (*) is only asserted ('on conclut aisément'). Surjectivity follows from the epimorphic family of the Ỹ → F being preserved by φ. Injectivity also needs φ to preserve epimorphisms and fibre products, applied to the kernel pair. This is routine but not spelled out.
Notation mismatch: (*) is written with Y̌ and Hom(Y̌, φ) ≅ φ(Ỹ). Here Y̌ must mean the functor Hom(Ỹ, −) on the topos. The text also passes silently between φ(Y) and φ(Ỹ).
The converse direction of 7.9.2, from (φ, ξ) to ψ, is not stated, only implied by 'équivaut'.

ideas.what: A fibre functor (point) of a topos of sheaves on a site with finite limits is pro-represented by the cofiltered system of objects (Y, ξ) of its category of elements.
ideas.modern_name: points of a topos = flat (filtering) functors / pro-representability of fibre functors
ideas.where_published: SGA 4 Exp. IV §6 (points of topoi, 6.8) and Exp. VIII §7

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typescript draft of standard SGA 4 material on points of topoi and of the étale topos, all of which was published. Its only interest is archival: it appears interleaved with the EGA VI plans.
transcription_corrections: 'à fortion' in the typescript is a typo for 'à fortiori'.
'aisement' should read 'aisément' (accent missing in the typescript).
In (*) and in 'Hom(Y̌, φ)' the object is typed as Y with a háček (Y̌), distinct from Ỹ (tilde) used for the associated sheaf. The transcription preserves this correctly.
'Au foncteur fibre ψ: E/Y → (Ens)': the subscript is /Y, i.e. E_{/Y}, as transcribed.
